rationale: Task instances are released and the environment, verifiers and Rule Agent run offline from cached records with no judge model. Source databases are fetched unversioned from PhysioNet, requirements are unpinned, and DeepSeek is queried via a live API (the model under test), so full pinning is not shown.

rationale: Table 2 documents each action and tool with effect and output fields, and per-action effects (time advance, read-only measure, memory write) are given. No machine-readable schema is shown and error returns are not documented in S1-S3. s5_reach true via the Appendix C system prompt, which restates that measure runs without advancing time (S5 chunks absent from packet).

quotes.text: instead return a ready-made label read from ground-truth annotations, causally clamped to the elapsed window.

rationale: README discloses that diagnostic tools are label stubs read from ground-truth annotations. No tool conformance tests are reported (tests cover verifiers and the environment). The agent prompts only call the output a ready-made label and do not say it is derived from ground truth, so the disclosure does not reach S5.

quotes.text: write appends a cursor-timestamped entry to memory, from which the final answer is assembled

rationale: Applicable because write commits a finding to an append-only ledger (a note-like report). The paper states which actions mutate state (write appends; measure does not advance time; skim advances the cursor). It does not state whether writes are executed or sandboxed, and does not explicitly score unsafe or unnecessary writes, though F1 implicitly penalises spurious ones.

quotes.text: Each whole recording is streamed online and scored by the task verifier at the end of the stream.
so rewards are rule-based rather than judge-based

rationale: Grader input is the answer assembled from the memory ledger, scored by deterministic verifiers, with the rule-based-not-judge-based rationale. No validation against labelled correct and incorrect outcomes with error rates is reported.

quotes.text: any view/tool request is clamped to `[·, cursor]` (no future signal)

rationale: Causal clamping of all tools and views to the elapsed signal is a leakage control on the agent channel. No private or held-out split (task answers are public in the repo) and no canary or provenance marker.
